# Private Tours vs Group Tours: Which is best?

Chris Choi

February 4, 2022

[Read 1 Comment](https://www.vviptravel.com/blog/private-tours-vs-group-tours#comments)

![Wearing Hanbok (Korean traditional clothes) during a tour in Seoul)](https://www.vviptravel.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/wearing-hanbok.jpg)

When planning your vacation to a new and exciting place, you want to make the most of it and ensure you get what you signed up for. But just like any foreign, exotic location, it can be daunting. Where to go? What to do? How do I get answers to all my questions?

That’s why most travellers book a tour to get their bearings and visit the top local spots. And, just like the rest of the world, when booking your tour in South Korea, you are confronted with 2 main options. Should I book a group tour or a private tour?

This post compares the pros and cons of booking a group vs a private tour when visiting Korea.

Table of Contents

Toggle

## Private tour pros

### Complete Freedom and flexibility

Personalised private tours give you total freedom and flexibility. The tour itinerary and schedule is entirely focused and planned around you. Everything is catered around your tastes, including places to visit, things to do, types of activities you’ll enjoy and even the menu.

With a personal tour, there are no rigid pre-planned itineraries that you need to accommodate, although we do offer a suggested course to get you started if you don’t already have something in mind.

### Explore at your own pace

Have you ever found yourself on a group tour, enjoying a particular spot, but then times up, and you have to move on before you’re ready to accommodate the group’s itinerary? One of the benefits of private tours is that you can go at your own pace.

If you’re not enjoying a particular location or activity, you can skip it and move on to something else. But, on the other hand, if you are thoroughly enjoying a particular place or experience, you don’t need to worry about time limits and getting back to the bus.

In short, if time is important to you, then a private tour is probably what you’re looking for.

### More exclusivity

While group tours rely on buses filled with other travellers, private tours allow you to choose who will accompany you on your trip. Whether travelling alone, with family or friends you can enjoy more privacy and comfort.

In addition, this makes private tours ideal for special occasions like honeymoons, wedding anniversaries, birthdays, or just travelling with friends and family on vacation.

### Special care and assistance

Having your own personal guide and transportation provides you with that extra special care and attention. This is especially helpful if you are travelling with young children, elderly relatives, disabled travellers, those with medical conditions, special needs or mobility issues.

Your guide will be able to accommodate your dietary needs better and plan around you, while your driver will transport you door to door to make you as comfortable as possible.

Without other travellers to take care of, your guide will solely focus on you and your travel companions’ needs.

### Your own personal tap of local knowledge

Having your own personal guide means there is no competing with other travellers to get the attention of your guide or to have your questions answered. Instead, you’ll have access to a tap of local culture and knowledge.

Find out everything you want to know, get recommendations on foods to try, things to do and places to visit. In addition, you can get to know a real Korean local who can introduce you to places off the beaten track.

## Private tour cons

### Cost (sometimes)

Private tours are usually considered much more expensive due to the luxury, convenience and personal attention they offer. While there is some truth in this, as personal tours can often be more expensive than group tours, this isn’t always the case.

When travelling within a group of family or friends, booking a private tour can be more economical than the per-seat cost of individually booking everyone on a group tour.

Therefore, it is worth comparing the entire cost of a group tour and private tour over the per seat or individual cost of booking one person.

### Not a good option for meeting new people

If you are travelling alone and looking to meet fellow travellers for companionship, this option is probably not a good idea.

On the other hand, a group tour would offer you more opportunities to meet others while exploring Korea.

## Group tour pros

### Best for those on a tight budget

As one would expect, group tours usually offer the cheapest option for those on a tight budget. Economies of scale are the main factor at play here, where travellers can benefit from the savings associated with sharing resources.

One thing to bear in mind is that this does depend on the number of people in your party. For example, those travelling in a group of friends or family may find that the cost of a private tour can work out the same or even cheaper when compared with the per-person cost of a group tour.

### You can meet new people along the way

It’s not always easy to make friends and meet new people while travelling alone. For this reason, group tours can offer you an opportunity to connect with fellow travellers.

Since group tours are not restricted to specific people, they usually comprise a mix of travellers from all over the world who can speak the same language as you. It can also be an excellent way to break the ice and give you a common topic of conversation.

If you are looking to make acquaintances and potentially new friends during your stay, then group tours are probably the better option for you.

## Group tour cons

### You will have to follow a rigid schedule

While group tours operated by quality travel agencies are usually well designed and encompass the experience international visitors seek, they still come with a rigid itinerary that needs to be followed.

This is to ensure the group’s satisfaction is met overall rather than the satisfaction of the individual. Therefore group tours include fixed dates, times, itineraries and stop durations to ensure every activity advertised is ticked off.

### Forced shopping or other activities

Unlike our group [DMZ tours with no forced shopping](https://www.vviptravel.com/dmz-tours), group tours often include a mandatory shopping stop. This is included to offset the tour cost and bring down the cost of the tour participation fee.

While this isn’t an issue for most people as it usually just involves a quick stop on the way to or from an experience, bargain bucket tour companies can take this to another level.

Therefore, you should be aware of group tours that offer considerably lower prices than their competition as you may spend a lot more time shopping, or even worse be subject to hard selling.

### You will have to share transportation with other travellers

Group tours usually start by going around and picking up other fellow travellers before the tour starts and then include numerous stops on the way back. In addition, waiting for others to return to the bus at the agreed meeting time can be frustrating for some when you are ready to move on.

If you find yourself frustrated by these small inefficiencies, then a group tour is not for you. It is also one of the significant advantages of booking a private tour, so you may wish to consider that option.

## Pros and Cons Checklist Summary

Choose a Group Tour if

You’re on a tight budget

Want to meet new people

Are travelling alone or with a friend

Have few or no special requirements

Comes with a fixed itinerary

Includes forced shopping stops

Need to share transport and resources

Choose a Private Tour if

Want more flexibility or a custom itinerary

You’re short on time

Need special care and attention

Travelling with the elderly or infants

Travelling with family or friends

Looking for the most comfort/luxury

Are more expensive (sometimes)

Not a good choice for meeting new people

## How to make the most out of a private tour

After booking your private tour on your preferred tour dates, think about what you want to get out of your experience. The more information you can provide us with, the better we can tailor your tour and experiences to your needs and tastes.

Try to answer some of these questions and write down your answers. Then let us know, and discuss them with your [private tour guide](https://www.vviptravel.com/private-tour-guide) at the start of your tour:

- Do you already have a few ideas of things you would like to see/do during your trip?
- What kind of experience would you like to have (active, historic, palaces, scenic, food, markets, shopping, city tour, children’s activities)?
- Do you have any specific requirements?
- Are you travelling with the elderly, disabled or any young children?
- Do you wish to attend a specific event?
- The more information you can provide, the better we can tailor your tour around you.

If you have difficulty answering any of the above, do not fret. Your guide can make plenty of suggestions for you. In addition, apart from any pre-made bookings for experiences, your guide can be quite flexible and, in discussion with you, can alter your itinerary on the day based on the weather and what you feel like at the moment.

## Frequntly Asked Questions (FAQs)

Here are some of the most common questions about group tours vs private tours. If you still have any unanswered questions, please drop us a comment below.

### What does a private tour mean?

A private tour means that the tour’s itinerary is completely tailored around you and that the resources included are for your use only. A private tour usually consists of a personal tour guide, choice of private vehicle and chauffeur driver.

### What does a group tour mean?

Group tours are open tours that allow anyone to sign up and participate in a local experience with others. These tours usually comprise of travellers visiting from various countries who can all speak a common language. Through sharing resources, they take advantage of economies of scale to reduce the cost of participation and are a great way to meet new people while travelling.

### Are group tours cheaper?

Group tours are usually cheaper than private tours but often cost a little more than independent travel, although they can sometimes still work out cheaper. However, you should also consider that tours save you a lot of time in research, organisation and booking your trip and activities.

### How do private tours work?

Private tours are designed around your desires, tastes and schedule. If you already have a list of things you want to do, the tour agency can organise an itinerary and manage the details. Alternatively, tour agencies can provide a pre-made itinerary as a starting point which can then be revised based on your feedback.

### Should I travel solo or with a group?

Group travel offers many benefits such as saving time, providing opportunities to meet fellow travellers, learn about the culture and local points of interest. In addition, while group tours may initially appear more expensive, they can actually work out cheaper when adding up all the individual expenses of travelling solo, including transportation and entry fees.

### Why are private tours better?

Private tours give you the freedom to choose what you want to do and when. You don’t have to consider the needs of other travellers, which provides you with far more room for flexibility and changes to your itinerary at every step of the way. The flexibility and freedom to make the most of your time are why most people choose private tours over group tours.

## How to book our personalised tours and chauffeur services

For those simply looking to book a half-day or full-day customised tour with a local and knowledgable private guide, we have created [standard private tour packages](https://www.vviptravel.com/private-tour-guide) that you can easily book online for your convenience.

However, if you have any questions, require further assistance or have very specific requirements which require prior planning then you can fill out our [Private tour enquiry form](https://www.vviptravel.com/private-tour-guide#private-tour-enquiry-form) and we’ll be happy to help.

### How to book a private tour with us online

Our online tour package is great for those who just need a private guide or those who need a private guide with transportation.

1. Visit our [private tour booking page](https://www.vviptravel.com/private-tour-guide#book-a-private-tour-in-korea) and select either our half-day or full-day private tour option. In our example on the right, we chose the full-day tour.
2. On the booking form on the right-hand side of the page, choose the date you wish to take the tour.
3. Once the date is chosen, you’ll be able to select a start time.
4. Select the number of people who will join the tour.
5. (Optional) Under “Additional Services”, you can add chauffeured transportation by choosing a vehicle.
6. After choosing all the options, the booking form will calculate and display the total at the top in Korean Won.
7. Click the blue “Add to cart” button to proceed and pay online using a secure third-party payment gateway or choose our “pay on tour” option.
8. That’s it! We’ll be in touch soon to confirm your order and arrange the details.

![Screenshot of VIP Travel's private tour online booking form.](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='370'%20height='730'%20viewBox='0%200%20370%20730'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

### How to book our chauffeured transportation service online

This online package is great for those who only need private vehicle transportation and a driver.

![Screenshot of VIP Travel's chauffeur service online booking form.](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='370'%20height='730'%20viewBox='0%200%20370%20730'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

1. Visit our [Korea chauffeur service booking page](https://www.vviptravel.com/chauffeur-service) and select either our half-day or full-day private transportation option. In our example on the right, we chose the full-day option.
2. On the booking form on the right-hand side of the page, choose the date you require the service.
3. Once the date is chosen, you can select a pick-up time.
4. Select the number of people in your group.
5. Under “Additional Services”, you must choose the type of vehicle you require. Each vehicle comes with an experienced safe driver.
6. After choosing all the options, the booking form will calculate and display the total at the top in Korean Won.
7. Click the blue “Add to cart” button to proceed and pay online using a secure third-party payment gateway or choose our “pay on tour” option.
8. That’s it! We’ll be in touch soon to confirm your order and arrange the details.

### How to book our airport pick-up/drop-off service online

This online service is for those who require one-way airport transportation (pick-up or drop-off). If you require a pick-up and drop-off simply book each journey separately.

1. Visit our [airport transportation service booking page](https://www.vviptravel.com/tours/airport-transfer).
2. On the booking form on the right-hand side of the page, choose the date you require the service.
3. Select the number of people in your group.
4. Under “Additional Services”, you must choose the vehicle type you require. Each vehicle includes a professional, safe driver.
5. If you would like an escort please select the “Licensed Guide” checkbox and enter the number of guides you require.
6. After choosing all the options, the booking form will calculate and display the total at the top in Korean Won.
7. Click the blue “Add to cart” button to proceed and pay online using a secure third-party payment gateway or choose our “pay on tour” option.
8. That’s it! We’ll be in touch soon to confirm your order and arrange your pick-up.

![Screenshot of VIP Travel's airport transfer service online booking form](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='370'%20height='700'%20viewBox='0%200%20370%20700'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

### How to get private tour consultation, or help booking your tour

Simply fill in our [private tour enquiry form](https://www.vviptravel.com/private-tour-guide#private-tour-enquiry-form) with as much information as you can and we’ll get back to you as soon as possible. See an example below.

![VIP Travel Private Tour Enquiry Form](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1024'%20height='580'%20viewBox='0%200%201024%20580'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

## Conclusion

As you can see, there are many benefits to choosing both group and personal tours. Which is best for you really depends on what you are looking to get out of your trip and who you are travelling with.

So what which option will you choose? Let us know in the comments below.

web.title: How to choose between guided tours or independent travel
web.description: Here are my thoughts on for whom they are best suited, and some pros and cons about taking a group tour over organising your own independent travel.
web.markdown:
[Skip to Content](https://www.bloggeratlarge.com/guided-tours-v-independent-travel-pros-cons/#content)

If you’re considering booking yourself onto a guided group tour but are a bit unsure about whether group travel is right for you, here are my thoughts on for whom they are best suited, and some pros and cons about taking a group tour over organising your own independent travel.

But first a bit about me, I have been a professional travel writer since 2000 and travel blogger since 2006, launching this blog in 2009. I started hosting tours for my readers in 2017 – but I realise hosted tours aren’t for everyone!

I have also written up a [sneaky, easy way to plan your own itineraries](https://www.bloggeratlarge.com/a-sneaky-easy-way-to-create-your-own-travel-itinerary/), without all the research and while barely lifting a finger, in this post.

![](https://www.bloggeratlarge.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/Lunch-by-Colosseum-Rome.jpg)Hidden gems in Rome

### Haven't got time to finish this post now?

Save it for later and I'll email it to you!

Over the past nearly 20 years (and previously when I was living and working in London for five years) I did plenty of independent travel with friends and family. Cheap and cheerful trips through to high-end luxury resorts, self-driving tours and fully organised ones as well.

I’m going to admit though, I was never much of a “back packer”. I’ve always said I am more duvet than sleeping bag and I don’t think I’ve ever stayed in a hostel in my life!

Mind you, back in the 90s it was cheap to get around in Europe and the UK where BnBs (no such thing as Air BnB!) were priced around £15 per night. So sharing rooms with strangers was not necessary (nor desirable!)

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='759'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20759'%3E%3C/svg%3E)All masked up ready to fly!

_I once stayed in a cliff top villa in Corfu with a friend for £10 per night and we ate at the local taverna every day in between swimming and sun bathing. Oh how times have changed. Now young people couch surf and stay in strangers lounges! \*Shudder_

Then in 2017 I embarked on [hosting my own small group tours](https://www.bloggeratlarge.com/blogger-at-large-tours/) to take like-minded people, who want to join me to some of my favourite places.

I did this for a couple of reasons, 1) I have been to some incredible places and been shown around by the destination marketers who revealed behind-the-scenes places to see, eat, sleep and things to do that I would never think of doing if left to my own devices, so I wanted to take people to places I’ve loved.

And 2) I thought it would be fun and provide another income stream, which as a blogger is more like an income trickle! And as long as they remain fun I’ll keep doing them.

![Leading my group in Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='779'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20779'%3E%3C/svg%3E)With some of my group learning history from our guide in Italy

**_But I’ll admit that tour groups aren’t for everyone, so below is a quick list of who tours are best suited to and who would probably hate them!_**

## When is group travel right for me?

### If you’re busy

If you’re too busy to organise an extensive trip (because a 2-week trip in Italy, for example, could take several months of organising!), a tour could be right for you.

All the admin is done for you. The day to day itinerary is sorted, the hotels are arranged, transfers from airports to hotels and coaches or trains around the country, tickets into the museums and attractions will no doubt be VIP access so you don’t need to wait in line for hours. You will probably also have several meals included and the best places to see in each town will be sorted out for you.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='758'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20758'%3E%3C/svg%3E)Enjoying a winery lunch in Central Otago with a couple on my tour

### Single traveler looking for company

If you don’t have any one to travel with, a group tour with like-minded people could be great for you.

On my own tours I have found the majority of my guests tend to be between 50 and 82 years old and most have been single women, the occasional couple thrown in for good measure! All of them have found someone they gel with and have kept in touch since.

Several of them have even joined me on a second, third and even fourth tour, which means a lot.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='750'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20750'%3E%3C/svg%3E)Taking the team for a stroll in China

### You love to learn new things

What you’ll also get on a guided tour are the guides! That means that if you have a penchant for learning a little history, or hearing how something was made or painted or sculpted, or you like other kinds of information like a fascination with flora and fauna, you’ll like having local guides with you.

![Group tour on Ha Long Bay](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='695'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20695'%3E%3C/svg%3E)We’re off on the kayaks and fishing boats in Ha Long Bay

### Safety conscious

This is a good reason to take a tour to somewhere that might not be as “safe” (where is safe now days though, right?) as English speaking countries or a place you know well.

On a tour you’ll have local guides and drivers and if anything goes awry there is someone there to help you deal with it. On my first tour, which was to Vietnam, one of my guests ate something that didn’t agree with her and I ended up cleaning up poo and taking her to a local private hospital (travel insurance is imperative) where she stayed for two nights. I was able to help sort out her insurance and visited her a few times with clothes and her cell phone charger so she could keep in touch with family.

### You get inside knowledge

If you join a tour led by people who know the city/country well, they will take you to places you wouldn’t find otherwise – or certainly not without a lot of research!

On my tour to New Orleans (I have now been there seven times) one of the highlights was a casual off-the-beaten-track Monday night jazz night in the back yard of a local musician, complete with beans and rice and plenty of gin and tonics!

You’ll also be able to pick the brains of your local guides for things like where to change money, where to get laundry done, where to find great tapas…

### Good if you’re on a tight time frame

If you have limited time for your vacation then a tour could also be right for you. If you choose a tour that visits the cities you really want to see, like Rome, Florence and Venice for example, a tour that features those cities will make life simple and have all the transport, accommodation and entry tickets organised.

## Things to **look for** before you book a group tour

### Single supplement

A single supplement is often charged for someone travelling alone and wanting their own room rather than sharing with their partner/friend or a fellow traveler.

On my tours I cost them up as a single person per room, but if they bring a friend or partner, that person comes at nearly half price as the room cost is covered by the first person.

### Size of the group tour

This is very important. I can think of nothing worse than being on one of those big 40+ groups being ferried around on massive coaches. This is when group travel can be a total pain, you’ll always be waiting for someone! However, they are great for seeing loads of things in a short amount of time and meeting lots of people.

I only run small group tours. I want mine to be exclusive and boutique. I don’t want to compete with the big tour companies. The most I have ever hosted was 22, and that’s plenty big enough for me! Usually they’re around 14-16.

![Cyclo tour in Vietnam](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='750'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20750'%3E%3C/svg%3E)Taking my group of 11 on cyclos in Hanoi

### Travel insurance

Travel insurance won’t be included in the group tour cost and on my tours it’s imperative (for obvious reasons). Just make sure that you’re not doing any activities that you might not be covered for, or if you’re unsure, check with your insurer.

### Free time

Over the years I have been hosted in many places by PR companies and destination marketers and some itineraries have been packed. Sometimes too packed. Read through your tour itinerary to see how exhausting it’s going to be.

Are you moving every couple of days? Do you have early starts? Are you expected to join the group for dinner each night? Are there mornings or afternoons free for you to rest, shop, explore on your own? I try and make sure we have a nice balance of seeing lots of things v relaxing.

![Private guide in Italy](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='750'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20750'%3E%3C/svg%3E)Our guide at the Colosseum in Rome was brilliant and brought it to life!

## When group travel might not be right for you

### You like to go with the flow

If you hate structure, then a group tour might not be right for you! The itinerary will be planned and guides will be booked. You may choose not to join some activities, but you also don’t want FOMO so you’ll feel obliged to join the group!

### You have unique interests

Or you don’t have unique interests! If you just want to potter around ancient towns left to your own devices, or maybe you’re wanting to trace an ancestor, then a tour won’t be right for you. Of course you could always join a tour then add on a few days for those things on your own.

### You love planning your vacation

Some people are planners. I get that. On a group tour all the planning is done for you. While it might still be interesting for planners and Googly researchers to see what each day will bring, what the hotels and attractions are like and online recommendations for where to eat in your free time, some people love to do it all from scratch.

### You’re on a tight budget

Group travel might cost a little more than making your own travel plans. Even with a travel agent taking their commission. But all the extras you get (not to mention the time saving – how much is your time worth?!) need to be weighed up against your budget.

### Independent travel planning hack!

If you are going to make your own travel plans, a good place to start is to read some group tour itineraries for the places you plan to visit to save a whole load of time!

_There! I hope that’s helped._

**[See my latest small group tours here >>](https://www.bloggeratlarge.com/blogger-at-large-tours/)**

* * *

![Croatia small group tour](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20width='1000'%20height='423'%20viewBox='0%200%201000%20423'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

# Private Tour or Group Tour: Which One Is Right for You? \| Complete Guide for Travelers

- [November 29, 2025](https://www.east-site.com/2025/11/29/)
- [Julia Shin](https://www.east-site.com/author/jshin/)
- Topic: [Guided Tours](https://www.east-site.com/blog/guided-tours/)

![5 stans tour private tour and small group tours](https://www.east-site.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/5StansTour1-2.jpg)

Choosing between a private tour and a group tour is one of the most important decisions when planning a trip—especially if you’re exploring unique destinations like Central Asia, the Silk Road, or remote cultural regions. Both options come with their own style, atmosphere, and advantages. This guide will help you understand the difference and decide what fits your travel personality.

* * *

## What’s the Difference?

A private tour gives you full flexibility: you choose the pace, timing, and overall flow. A group tour, on the other hand, offers a structured journey with a small group of 4–15 travelers who share the same route and experiences. Both formats are excellent—it’s just a matter of choosing what aligns with your expectations.

* * *

## Why Choose a Private Tour?

Our private tours can be arranged from just 2 people, with an additional $1,000 per person. This option turns your trip into a fully personalized experience.

1. You Control the Schedule

Private tours let you choose when to start your day, when to stop for lunch, how long to spend at each sight, and when to rest. No pressure to follow anyone else’s pace.
2. Maximum Comfort and Privacy

You travel only with your partner, family, or friends.

No crowded buses, no waiting for late travelers, no adjusting to different energy levels. It’s intimate, calm, and perfectly tailored to your mood that day.
3. Flexibility on the Route

Feel like spending an extra hour at the bazaar? Want to skip a museum and go for a scenic viewpoint instead?

Your guide adjusts the tour based on your preferences throughout the day.
4. Individual Attention

Private guiding means deeper insights, detailed storytelling, and more time for questions. Whether you love history, photography, food, or nature, the guide shapes the tour to your interests.

* * *

## Why Choose a Group Tour?

Our group tours range from 4 to 15 people, which keeps the experience comfortable, social, and fun.

1. Budget-Friendly

Group tours are more affordable because costs are shared among travelers. Perfect if you’re price-conscious but still want a full, high-quality program.
2. Built-In Group Dynamics & Shared Motivation

Traveling with a group naturally creates a sense of rhythm: the group moves together, encourages each other, and keeps the momentum alive.

It’s perfect for travelers who enjoy a structured atmosphere and feel more inspired and energized when experiencing new places alongside others.

There’s always someone to chat with, laugh with, and share impressions with — making even long rides or early mornings feel easier and more fun.
3. Social Connections & Unexpected Friendships

Group tours attract solo travelers, couples, and friends.

They’re a fantastic way to meet new people—and yes, sometimes even your future partner. We’ve had travelers join the tour alone and leave as a couple. It doesn’t happen every day, but the magic does occur!
4. Shared Experiences = More Fun

Exploring with others often makes the journey more energetic and emotional. You laugh together, try new foods together, and create memories that stay with you long after the trip is over.

* * *

## So, Which One Is Right for You?

If you’re dreaming of a journey where the schedule bends around your mood, where you travel at your own pace and enjoy full privacy, then a private tour will feel like a perfect fit. It’s ideal for couples, families, or anyone who wants a more intimate and flexible experience.

But if you love the energy of traveling with others, enjoy meeting new people, want a more budget-friendly option, and feel motivated by the shared excitement of a small group, then a group tour will be exactly what you’re looking for. It’s social, dynamic, and often full of surprises — sometimes even romantic ones.

In the end, both formats offer unforgettable adventures. The best choice is simply the one that matches your travel style and the kind of memories you want to create.
